ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZf87QA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDHG2U", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 47, "title": "Correct V30MZ flags after successful word DIV and IDIV", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `2669967f37dbbb65410ce8dcc496c1d1689a1693`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:1048` clears only OF after successful division, preserving the other arithmetic flags. Independent WonderSwan CPU experiments specify different word-division behavior. Incorrect flags can change subsequent conditional branches across the WonderSwan family; commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

Static reproduction, not executed during planning: `F7 F3` with DX:AX=`0000:0006`, BX=`0002`, FLAGS=`F002` produces quotient 3 and remainder 0 but retains FLAGS=`F002`; expected FLAGS are `F042`.

## Expected outcome

For successful word unsigned `F7 /6` and signed `F7 /7` division:

- Clear AF, CF, OF, PF and SF.
- Set ZF exactly when the remainder is zero and the quotient's least significant bit is one.
- Preserve quotient/remainder results, unrelated control flags, operand memory, decoding, bus accounting and shared-clock scheduling.

Apply the same semantics to emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations, independently of graphics mode.

## Context

Local HEAD and inspected remote main match the baseline; the checkout is clean. The open Issues/PR collection is empty. Inspection of all 46 closed entries found no equivalent completed correction. Issues #43 and #45 explicitly left division separate.

The [NEC V30MZ preliminary manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), §3.1.5, leaves several division flags undefined and specifies cleared overflow. Undefined does not establish preservation. The pinned [WSCPUTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/README.md) supplies the console-specific successful-word rules. Its [independent calculators](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm#L5607) calculate unsigned expectations from line 5607 and signed expectations from line 5822. These are inspected experiment sources; no physical execution or per-model measurement log was independently inspected. Applying register-tested semantics to mapped operands uses the documented common instruction forms.

Correction record: replace the implementation assumption that clearing OF while retaining the remaining arithmetic flags sufficiently models successful word division. Record the corrected requirements, sources and rationale; retain the valid word-OF requirement and prior regression obligations.

Scope is the existing successful word-division path and its native/Wasm/browser coverage. Byte DIV multiplication-history producers, byte IDIV flags, signed exceptional results, fault flags/classification, decimal adjustment and absolute timing remain separate unresolved work. This task does not establish complete CPU or commercial-game readiness.

[Saved #45 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/2669967f37dbbb65410ce8dcc496c1d1689a1693/docs/issue-45-validation.md) reports 131 core tests, 20 integration tests, one adapter test and complete Chromium suites passing. It also records two smoke failures before a later review-node pass. These are reported results, not planning-time reruns. Existing division tests are present but principally assert results, fault delivery and OF clearing.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Document the assumption correction, exact word-division flag rules, model applicability and experimental limits. Implement both forms through ordinary decoding without changing byte division or fault classification.
- [ ] Add independent literal quotient/remainder/full-FLAGS vectors under contrasting incoming arithmetic and control flags. Cover zero, odd/even quotients, zero/nonzero remainders, unsigned high-word dividends, signed operand combinations and unambiguous successful boundary cases. Include negative odd quotients with zero remainder to distinguish the unusual ZF rule from normal SZP calculation. Expectations must not call the production flag helper.
- [ ] Exercise register divisors, accumulator/divisor aliases and aligned/odd mapped RAM, ROM and SRAM divisors with segment overrides. Check sampled operands, unchanged source memory and unrelated state, exact continuation, following conditional branches and existing access/execution accounting. Confirm returned costs advance shared devices once through the normal machine path.
- [ ] Cover emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations, Color/Crystal mono and color modes, and runtime mode transitions. Record an actual pre-fix focused-test failure and original native-probe failure, followed by corrected passes. Preserve existing divide-fault, byte-division, multiplication, shift/rotate, prefix, interrupt, HALT and DMA regressions.
- [ ] Add an original source-included CC0 probe using the existing fixture tooling. Native and production Chromium/Wasm checks must compare actual CPU-written results, full FLAGS and branch observations for both forms on every model and fresh restart. Invalidate stale completion and use fresh execution markers so retained saves cannot satisfy acceptance.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then the complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` suites sequentially against the production preview. Preserve three-model gates, firmware-free startup, video/input/frame continuity, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/EEPROM and browser save integrity.
- [ ] Update hardware-support/provenance documentation and record actual commands, failures, resolutions, passes and unperformed checks. The Coordinator reviews the final diff against every checkbox before merge; retain prior acceptance and distinguish bounded emulator evidence from commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Baseline production-Chromium discrimination, additional browser engines, lawful additional software and physical-console comparisons. None were performed during planning; none requires human confirmation or blocks merge.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
